findings.verifierReasoning: The source's opening qualification is an independent eligibility condition of the (g) exception. The proposed IR omits both the property-type limitation (real and/or tangible personal) and the acquisition-timing limitation (after the Closing Date). A compliance engine built on this IR could conclude that a Lien on intangible property (for example, receivables acquired in an acquisition) or on property acquired before the Closing Date is permitted under (g) as long as the origin test, proviso (A), and the 80% test are met, whereas the source text unambiguously confines (g) to real and/or tangible personal Property acquired after the Closing Date. This changes the scope of the permission, so the discrepancy is material.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The rule's gatedBy AND consists only of: (1) the OR of the clause (i)/(ii) origin predicates; (2) an UNSUPPORTED node for proviso (A); (3) the COMPARE for the 80% proviso (B). The conditions array repeats these same three items. No condition or expression requires that the Lien be on real and/or tangible personal Property, and no condition requires that the Property was acquired after the Closing Date.

findings.sourceEvidence: Liens upon real and/or tangible personal Property acquired after the Closing Date (by purchase, construction or otherwise) by the Parent Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries, each of which Liens either (i) existed on such Property before the time of its acquisition and was not created in anticipation thereof or (ii) was created solely for the purpose of securing Indebtedness representing, or incurred to finance, refinance or refund, the cost (including the cost of construction) of such Property and permitted by Section 7.2
findings.verifierReasoning: The source's opening qualification is an independent eligibility condition of the (g) exception. The proposed IR omits both the property-type limitation (real and/or tangible personal) and the acquisition-timing limitation (after the Closing Date). A compliance engine built on this IR could conclude that a Lien on intangible property (for example, receivables acquired in an acquisition) or on property acquired before the Closing Date is permitted under (g) as long as the origin test, proviso (A), and the 80% test are met, whereas the source text unambiguously confines (g) to real and/or tangible personal Property acquired after the Closing Date. This changes the scope of the permission, so the discrepancy is material.
